findingDetails.title: Four copies of the version-output classifier, and the installer's copy reads a different grammar than the three that agree
findingDetails.evidence: parseOpencodeVersion is line-identical in opencode-version.mjs:104-130, opencode-version.cjs:142-163 and opencode-version-battery.cjs:146-171, each with its own VERSION_PATTERN constant and the same major===1/major===2 mapping. The shell classify_version does not use that pattern: the v1 branch requires a bare 1.x.y (setup.sh:85) while the v2 branch requires the literal 'opencode ' prefix (setup.sh:89), whereas the shared pattern admits an optional leading word and an optional v/V. The asymmetry matches observed output today (install-and-versions.md:263 records v1 bare, v2 as 'opencode v2.0.32'), so the divergence is latent, not live. The two Node resolvers have also drifted apart behaviorally: the .cjs carries an opencode2-then-opencode fallback vocabulary (opencode-version.cjs:35) that the .mjs lacks, returning 'unknown' when the name does not resolve on PATH (opencode-version.mjs:152).
findingDetails.userImpact: The third-version cost is paid four times across four grammars, one of which is already different; a banner-shape change in a supported version silently splits the installer's answer from the dispatcher's, and nothing fails.
findingDetails.scopeProof: rg -n "VERSION_PATTERN|major === 1" over .skilled returns exactly the three Node copies and no shared module. rg -n "opencode-version" filtered to require/import shows two live dispatch paths on two separate resolvers: dispatch-rule-checks.mjs:12 imports resolveOpencodeVersionSync from the .mjs, fanout-run.cjs:19 requires resolveOpencodeBinary from the .cjs.
findingDetails.recommendation: One shared family classifier consumed by both Node resolvers and the battery, plus one fixture corpus (bare, name-prefixed, v-prefixed, prefixed-and-v) asserted through the classifier and through the shell script, so drift fails a test. That corpus is also the mechanism that makes a third version one table row.
findingDetails.confidence: high on the duplication and the grammar divergence (read directly from source); medium on the no-parity-test component, which rests on test inventories rather than an exhaustive read of every test file
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: An existing cross-classifier parity test that feeds each classifier the same outputs would refute the no-parity-test component; the grammar divergence would still stand.

findingDetails.title: The rule engine's 'applies to both families' test is a literal v1-and-v2 conjunction, so a third family silently changes which rules keep blocking severity
findingDetails.evidence: dispatch-rule-checks.mjs:305 defaults appliesTo to ['v1','v2']; :306 computes appliesToBoth = includes('v1') && includes('v2'); :319 downgrades a violation to warn only when version === 'unknown' && !appliesToBoth. The predicate asks whether a rule mentions v1 and v2, not whether it covers every supported family. Those are the same question only while the supported set is exactly two: with a v3, a rule scoped to v1+v2 keeps appliesToBoth true and keeps blocking severity on an unknown-version dispatch although it says nothing about v3, while a rule scoped to v1+v3 is downgraded.
findingDetails.userImpact: The documented unknown-version downgrade stops matching the code's intent and fails in both directions at once, fail-open for one rule set and fail-closed for another, discovered by a dispatch that behaves unexpectedly rather than by a check.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The family set is spelled out as literals in at least five source files and exported by none: opencode-version-battery.cjs (30 occurrences incl. const FAMILIES = ['v1','v2'] at :52, used for arg validation at :207 and the run loop at :499), opencode-version.cjs (4), dispatch-rule-checks.mjs (4), fanout-run.cjs (3), hard-rules.json (6). No module exports SUPPORTED_FAMILIES.
findingDetails.recommendation: Export one SUPPORTED_FAMILIES from the shared classifier and derive both the default and the coverage predicate from it, so the downgrade condition becomes 'the rule covers every supported family' rather than 'the rule mentions v1 and v2'.
findingDetails.confidence: high on the code shape; the impact is prospective by construction, since nothing misbehaves until a third family exists
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A SUPPORTED_FAMILIES-style shared constant discovered elsewhere in the tree that :305-319 already consumes would refute it.

detail: Three Node copies of parseOpencodeVersion are line-identical (mjs:104-130, cjs:142-163, battery:146-171); the shell classifier at opencode-setup.sh:81-95 uses a different grammar that mirrors observed output today (v1 bare, v2 'opencode v2.0.32'), so the divergence is latent rather than live and R4-P2-001 stays at P2. The version family is a closed literal pair in at least five source files and exported by none.
